questions.prompt: About how many times wider is the Sun than Earth?
options: About 2 times
About 109 times
About 1,000 times
About the same size
questions.explanation: The Sun's radius is about 696,000 km while Earth's is about 6,371 km — roughly 109 times wider. More than a million Earths would fit inside the Sun's volume.
questions.misconception: Textbook diagrams often draw the Sun only a few times bigger than the planets so everything fits on the page, which makes it easy to underestimate the Sun's true dominance.

options: The distance light travels in one year
The average distance from Earth to the Sun, about 150 million km
The diameter of the Sun
The distance across the whole solar system
questions.explanation: One AU is the average Sun–Earth distance, about 150 million km. It is the standard ruler astronomers use for distances inside the solar system.
questions.misconception: AU and light-year get mixed up often — a light-year is the distance light travels in a year (about 9.5 trillion km) and is used for distances to other stars, while the AU is the Sun–Earth distance and is used inside the solar system.

questions.prompt: Why do most textbook diagrams of the solar system not show true scale?
options: True scale would make the planets invisible specks separated by huge gaps
Artists do not know the real sizes
The Sun is too big to draw at any size
The planets change size every year
questions.explanation: At true scale the planets would be far too small to label and the gaps between them far too large, so diagrams compress the distances to stay readable — which quietly hides the real emptiness.
questions.misconception: Some learners assume the compressed diagram is accurate because it appears in a book. In reality it is a deliberate compromise: showing sizes and showing distances at the same time is physically impossible on one page.

questions.prompt: About how long does sunlight take to travel from the Sun to Earth?
options: About 8 seconds
About 8 minutes
About 8 hours
About 8 days
questions.explanation: Light travels at about 300,000 km per second, so the 150 million km trip from the Sun to Earth takes about 8 minutes. To Neptune it takes roughly 4–5 hours.
questions.misconception: Because the Sun is so close in drawings, it is easy to imagine sunlight arriving instantly — but the Sun's light you see right now left the Sun 8 minutes ago.

questions.prompt: In a true-to-scale view of the solar system, which statement is correct?
options: The planets are large and packed close together
The planets are tiny specks spread across vast empty distances
All eight planets are about the same size
The Sun is smaller than Jupiter
questions.explanation: At true scale, planets are minuscule compared with the Sun and with the distances between them — the solar system is mostly empty space.
questions.misconception: Space looks 'crowded' in diagrams, so it is easy to believe the solar system is packed with objects. In reality, if you shrank the Sun to a basketball, Earth would be a peppercorn about 30 m away.
